newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Religion not a factor in Java attacks - commission.
newsitem.headline: Religion not a factor in Java attacks - commission.

text.p: A member of Indonesia's official National Commission on Human Rights said on Tuesday that attacks by a Moslem mob on 25 churches in East Java last month were not triggered by religious tension.
"It is not a problem between religions. It is purely a criminal matter," Arnold Baramuli, a member of the commission investigating the attacks, told reporters after leaving a commission meeting.
But Baramuli, who is also a legislator for the ruling Golkar party, said the commission had not ruled out the possibility of a conspiracy behind the attacks.

An angry mob of Moslems burned down or damaged 25 churches in the town of Situbondo in East Java on October 10 after rumours spread that a man being tried for blaspheming Islam had escaped and taken refuge in a church.
Five people died in the violence.
Commission officials said on Tuesday it was not clear when the body would release its final report on the incident.
Police said on Wednesday that they had detained 54 people suspected of being involved in the riot in Situbondo, 160 km (100 miles) east of Indonesia's second-largest city, Surabaya.
Police said those detained would be taken to court.
